the following questions: How is the citizen-consumer represented in media and communications regulation?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the citizen-consumer is a discursive construct that has been used by Ofcom to justify its role in the media sector, to justify its role as a regulator, and to justify its role to the public as an advocate for the citizen.
the term “citizen-consumers” is not a useful concept, and that “citizens,” as a term, should not be conflated with “consumers.”
“citizen” is used in a variety of ways and that it is not possible to draw a clear line between “consumer” and “citizen.”
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
citizens are not consumers, and the citizen-consumer is a problematic concept for media and communications regulation.
citizens are being asked to do more than they are being asked to be.

The main takeaway from our work is that
citizens and consumers have different needs, which should be reflected in the regulatory regime.
